chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Abdullah ibn Amir, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about shortening the prayer. He said: 'If you are in a place where you hear the call to prayer, complete it; and if you are in a place where you do not hear the call to prayer, shorten it; and when you return from a journey, it is the same.'

key_terms.التَّقْصِيرِ: Shortening the prayer (performing 2 rak'ahs instead of 4)
key_terms.قَدِمْتَ مِنْ سَفَرٍ: When you return from a journey

ai.seo_question: When should a traveler shorten their prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the audible adhan as the primary criterion for determining the status of a traveler, reflecting the practical jurisprudence of the early Shia community. It highlights the scholarly principle that the boundary of the city or settlement, defined by the range of the call to prayer, dictates the transition between full (tamam) and shortened (qasr) prayers. This ruling underscores the importance of local communal markers in personal religious obligations.
